walkthroughs.body_html:
Lifestyle, Health & Risk — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Lifestyle, Health & Risk brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Lifestyle, Health & Risk.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A high blood level of which lipoprotein is associated with greater cardiovascular risk?
options: LDL
HDL
albumin
haemoglobin

mcqs.q: A study finds smokers have more heart attacks. This correlation:
options: does not by itself prove smoking causes heart attacks
proves smoking has no effect on the heart
means heart attacks cause smoking
shows the two are unrelated

mcqs.q: HDL is sometimes called 'good cholesterol' because it:
options: carries cholesterol from tissues back to the liver
deposits cholesterol into artery walls
is made only during exercise
replaces all LDL in the blood

mcqs.q: Does HDL cholesterol raise heart disease risk?
options: Atherosclerosis is an infection of the blood vessels.
No - HDL carries cholesterol back to the liver and is linked with lower risk; high LDL is linked with higher risk.
HDL turns into LDL once it reaches the arteries.
All cholesterol is bad and raises heart disease risk.

mcqs.q: Does a correlation between smoking and heart disease prove smoking causes it?
options: Correlation means the two variables are completely unrelated.
If two variables are correlated, one must cause the other.
A correlation alone does not prove causation; other factors could be involved, though further evidence can support a causal link.
HDL turns into LDL once it reaches the arteries.
Atherosclerosis is an infection of the blood vessels.
Atherosclerosis is simply the heart getting weaker with age.
It is the build-up of fatty plaques (atheroma) in artery walls, narrowing the lumen and restricting blood flow.
HDL turns into LDL once it reaches the arteries.

sequence.def: Artery lining injured by high BP or toxins
White blood cells gather at the damaged site
Cholesterol builds up under the lining
Fatty plaque hardens and bulges into the artery
Plaque ruptures; a clot can block the artery
